settings.label: Location
settings.help: Where to report the weather for

settings.label: Source
settings.help: Open-Meteo works anywhere. Environment Canada, MET Norway and the US National Weather Service each cover their own country, and add weather alerts.

OpenWeatherMap.question: Do you have an OpenWeatherMap API key?
OpenWeatherMap.text: OpenWeatherMap needs a key of your own. It's free: sign up at openweathermap.org and copy the key from the API keys page of your account.

Google Weather.question: Do you have a Google Weather API key?
Google Weather.text: Google Weather needs a key of your own, from a Google Cloud project with the Weather API turned on.

settings.label: OpenWeatherMap API key
settings.help: A new key can take a couple of hours to start working. Until then the widget says Invalid API key.

settings.label: Google Weather API key
settings.help: From Google Cloud, with the Weather API turned on for its project.

settings.label: Temperature
settings.help: Pressure follows it: hectopascals with Celsius, inches of mercury with Fahrenheit.

settings.label: Wind speed
settings.help: Automatic is km/h with Celsius and mph with Fahrenheit. Visibility follows it: kilometres or miles.

settings.label: Notify me about
settings.help: Weather alerts for this place, each shown once on this face's screens. In Canada and Norway, a yellow warning is moderate, orange severe, red extreme.

settings.label: Info order
settings.help: What matters most to you. The top one shows even on the smallest tile, and bigger tiles show more. Anything Open-Meteo has nothing for right now is skipped.
